ledger_excerpt:
From Shelley v. Kraemer, 334 U.S. 1, 19–20 (1948):
"These are not cases... in which the States have merely abstained from action, leaving private individuals free to impose such discriminations as they see fit. Rather, these are cases in which the States have made available to such individuals the full coercive power of government... We hold that in granting judicial enforcement of the private agreements in these cases, the States have denied petitioners the equal protection of the laws and that, therefore, the action of the state courts cannot stand."
